Vendored so bootstrap does not fetch GitHub.

- `pins.txt` is the sha256 list CI checks. `tools/check_vendor_pins.py` fails when a `vendor/*.whl` digest, its `.sha256` sidecar, or a `voxprint-common==` pin in `pyproject.toml` or a `requirements*.txt` file disagrees with that list.

- `voxprint_common-0.5.0-py3-none-any.whl`: the official v0.5.0 release asset from https://github.com/Mitroshenkov87/voxprint-common/releases/download/v0.5.0/voxprint_common-0.5.0-py3-none-any.whl (tag `v0.5.0`, tag commit e287e47655f9429ceb26bbc1b1454a9fd06afe2d; sha256 `a21e4309145e1eafb2c4f624890352154d955f316a407c312206092ea3814b2c`). The release has no combined SHA256SUMS file. Each archive has a `.sha256` sidecar, and that sidecar matches this digest and the GitHub asset digest. It bundles the same serial 9 signed model index as 0.4.1 (index head 15edeab, sha256 104742f9…f49e45f), the voxprint-model/1 schema (sha256 e46ae56a…5138), the voxprint-app-models/1 schema (sha256 ed451b99…c420), and the index public key (`mdl/data/index-public.pem`). CI, docs, release builds and the Windows setup install it. The `gui` extra pins `voxprint-common[ui]==0.5.0`. `SUITE_APPS` includes `model-forge`. `paths.read_home()` does not fall back to the legacy home (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Voxprint`, `~/.local/share/voxprint`); the Windows setup moves it first (`installer/windows/migrate-home.ps1`), and Model Forge only uses `paths.home()`-based helpers, which migrate on first use.
